origins.section: A Young Collection Costs What Survives, Not What Was Allocated
Each Collector Puts the Cost Somewhere: Pauses, Stalls or CPU
System.gc() Is a Request, and JVM Flags Decide What It Does
A Soft Cache Survives Collections While There Is Room, and Empties When an Allocation Doesn't Fit

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-batch-buffer: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-batch-buffer: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-batch-buffer: A Young Collection Costs What Survives: the 200,000 window's objects are copied, promoted and later found dead by concurrent marking and mixed collections; 14 pauses / 12.9 ms against 97 pauses / 1251.0 ms with the same allocation. Job B's buffer corresponds to the large window (by analogy).
recorded.prompt:q-low-pause-p99: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-low-pause-p99: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-low-pause-p99: Each Collector Puts the Cost Somewhere: single-generation ZGC marks the whole heap each cycle; the allocating thread stopped in Allocation Stall, about 20 ms at a time, 30 times per run. Reader noted the stem said 2 GB while the run used 1 GB; the stem was changed to 1 GB after this reading.
